refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.source: EuroLithos / GeoERA ornamental stone sheet 'Rojo Alicante', compiled by the Instituto Geologico y Minero de Espana (IGME); PDF metadata names J. Martinez Martinez (IGME), 2021. Physical properties page: apparent density (EN 1936) 2710 kg/m3, open porosity (EN 1936) 0.6 % vol, water absorption (EN 13755) 0.2 % wt. Sources given: IGME, RocMaquina, Levantina technical report. https://repository.europe-geology.eu/egdidocs/eurolithos/143.pdf
porosity.note: Confirmed. The sheet gives the place of origin as Monovar, Alicante, from the Cavarrasa quarries; La Romana appears only on its map. Its other entries are Jurassic (Dogger), biomicrite with calcite veins and stylolites, 98 % calcite. As a cross-check, 0.2 % wt x 2.71 = 0.54 % vol, which agrees with the EN 1936 porosity.

wettingDepth.note: As the Crema Marfil: a dense stone wets only its outer millimetre.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, J. Geophys. Res. Solid Earth 117, B08409, doi:10.1029/2011JB009041, abstract (read via https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1029/2011JB009041).
hurst.note: The exponents are confirmed from the abstract; the claim about limestone lithology is unverified (PDF unreadable). This is a transfer from fractures to a honed face.
